name: the world pays for the SIZE of the reported witness, not for finding one
condition: The organism searches a space of candidate objects for one that has a property the world can check. Finding one earns nothing by itself: fitness is paid according to how small the REPORTED object is under an order the WORLD declares in advance (not the organism's own), and only if the reported object still has the property when the world re-checks it. The organism has a budget of property checks per problem, shared between finding and reducing. A reported object that fails the re-check zeroes the problem.
capability_rewarded: Turning a first-found object with the property into a much smaller one that still has it, under someone else's notion of small, within a check budget -- and knowing when to stop and report rather than spend the budget.
world_requirements: a candidate space with a checkable property and a declared total order on candidates that the world owns and publishes before the run (Proteus: programs; still_solves; size_key = (node_count, depth, canonical))
ground truth for the minimum under that order on a subset of problems, by exhaustive enumeration where affordable (Proteus: minimal_by_enumeration to size 5 -- exists)
a per-problem check budget metered by the world (Techne's receipt has n_no_example_found_in_budget: the meter exists at the strategy level; the world must own it)
a starting object with the property handed to the organism (the honest use the consumer describes: shrink a KNOWN solution), so that finding and reducing are separable in the read-out
post-hoc re-check of the reported object by the world's own evaluator (still_solves is the world's, not the organism's)
vacuity_condition: Vacuous if first-found objects are already minimal under the world's order (then reducing earns nothing) -- eligibility count: the number of problems whose starting object is strictly larger than the enumerated minimum must be > 0 and reported (Techne: 45 scored, 24 with excess > 0 at the pin, so it is NOT vacuous on that fixture); ALSO vacuous if the world's order equals the organism's internal order (then the pressure measures nothing about choosing a notion of small); Proteus has stated in writing that the two orders differ.
trivial_shortcuts: report the starting object unchanged (closed: fitness is paid by size; zero reduction earns the floor)

enumerate the whole space up to the minimum (closed by the budget: enumeration to size 5 costs more checks than the budget allows on the larger problems -- the world must set the budget below enumeration cost and report it)
reduce under the organism's own order and hope it agrees (closed by the declared order: 24/45 disagreements at the pin is the measured cost of this shortcut)
return a smaller object that does not have the property (closed by the re-check and the zeroing)
cheat_control: Hand one copy of the organism the world's order as its own; hand another copy a deliberately different order (the ancestor's). The copy with the world's order must score at or above the other on every problem where the enumerated minimum is known; if it does not, the world is not rewarding reduction under ITS order and the pressure is not operational. Second arm: hand a copy the enumerated minimum directly -- it must reach the ceiling at zero reduction cost, or the scoring is broken.
negative_control: Problems where the starting object IS the enumerated minimum: every organism scores the same; a copy that 'reduces' anyway must be zeroed by the re-check or score identically.

hosting.owner: Proteus (substrate: proteus.boolean3.v0 programs, still_solves, size_key, minimal_by_enumeration -- all exist); executor half Vivarium (a kind with a check budget and a post-hoc re-check); K9: deliver to Vivarium + Proteus in one message
hosting.evidence: techne/acquisition/receipts/adapter_qualification-hypothesis-20260911T065703Z.json already runs this shape once, outside any world

notes: Stated without the mechanism. The ancestor's answer is a greedy descent under its own order over an encoding of the object; the consumer has already measured that this disagrees with the world's order in 24 of 45 cases. The pressure asks for reduction under the WORLD's order; how an organism gets there is its business. Read-out caution (K10): the two-copies cheat arm is one-sided only in the direction 'world-order copy scores lower' -- that proves the world does not reward its own order; equal scores prove nothing about choosing.
